test_title: SSC Selection Post Matric Level Official Paper (Held On: 28 June, 2023 Shift 1)
subject: general
question: A solid sphere has a surface area of 616 cm². This sphere is now cut into two hemispheres. What is the total surface area of one of the hemispheres?
solution:
Given:

The surface area of the sphere = 616 cm²

Formula Used:

Surface area of sphere = 4 × πr²

Volume of sphere = (4/3) × πr³

Calculation:

Surface area of sphere = 4 × πr²

⇒ 616 = 4 × (22/7) × r²

⇒ r² = 616 × 7/88

⇒ r² = 7 × 7

⇒ r = 7

TSA of one of the spheres = 2πr² + πr2

⇒ 3πr2

⇒ 3 × (22/7) × (7)²

⇒ 3 × 22 × 7

⇒ 462

∴ The **total surface area of one of the hemispheres** is 462 cm².
